sources.title: Cloudera container registry — manifest index platforms, queried 2026-08-24 from WindowsDesktop with the cluster's cloudera-creds pull secret
sources.summary: Direct GET /v2/<name>/manifests/<tag> with OCI-index Accept headers for every Cloudera image the WindowsDesktop cld-streaming cluster runs. All 16 are multi-arch OCI/Docker manifest indexes listing linux/amd64 AND linux/arm64. This is primary evidence — the Cloudera docs make no architecture statement (see r11-cso-arm64).

MiNiFi Java is not a container image on this registry (cloudera/cem-minifi-java, cloudera/minifi-java, cloudera/cem-minifi tag lists return no JSON); the fleet installs it as a tarball (minifi-2.24.08.0-19) — already proven on the aarch64 Jetson (NvidiaNano) with an aarch64 JRE
facts.evidence: CLAUDE-CHECKIN.md NvidiaNano block; registry tag-list probe 2026-08-24

sources.relevance_to_us: Retires the plan's largest Phase-0 risk: Cloudera Streaming Operators (CFM/NiFi 2.6 and 1.28, CSA/Flink 1.20.1 + SSB, CSM/Kafka 4.1 + Schema Registry + Surveyor, EFM 2.3.1, and the hardened postgres/kube-rbac-proxy thirdparty images) can be pulled natively on the aarch64 DGX Spark with the same chart versions WindowsDesktop runs. No upstream-image fallback is needed for any component. Still to prove on the box: they RUN under k3d on GB10 (CUDA-enabled node image, cgroup v2), not just pull.

open_questions: The images are arm64-native; whether NiFi's bundled native libs and CSA's Python/PyFlink wheels behave identically on GB10 is a run-time question for Phase 4, not a pull-time one.

load_bearing_claims.claim: All Cloudera Streaming Operators images used on WindowsDesktop are multi-arch with linux/arm64 (verified directly against container.repository.cloudera.com on 2026-08-24)
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: Decides whether F is 'Cloudera operators on the Spark' or 'upstream Apache images on the Spark'
